Job Summary:

The Centers of Excellence Program Manager will be a member of the Operations team within the Cancer Center Administration Office and will provide operational leadership and programmatic oversight for the Cancer Center’s Centers of Excellence. This position will initially be assigned to the Katy O. and Paul M. Rady Esophageal and Gastric Center of Excellence (Rady Center), with responsibility for overseeing Center operations and partnering with leadership to advance strategic, research, financial, philanthropic, educational, and programmatic priorities.

The Program Manager will serve as the primary operational partner to Center leadership and will be responsible for translating strategic priorities into actionable plans, managing complex programs and initiatives, monitoring progress toward Center goals, and ensuring effective coordination across faculty, staff, researchers, administrative partners, donors, and other stakeholders. The position is expected to operate with a high degree of independence and initiative, proactively identifying needs, risks, barriers, and opportunities and developing solutions that improve Center effectiveness and support continued growth.

The Program Manager will directly supervise program staff supporting the assigned Center of Excellence, including one Program Coordinator initially assigned to the Rady Center. The position will establish priorities, delegate responsibilities, and ensure effective operational and administrative support for Center leadership and initiatives.

As the Cancer Center’s Centers of Excellence portfolio grows and evolves, this position may be assigned responsibility for additional Centers of Excellence and will contribute to the development of shared processes, infrastructure, and best practices that support the Centers of Excellence model across the Cancer Center.

Key Responsibilities:

Center Operations and Strategic Management (40%)

Provide operational leadership for assigned Centers of Excellence and ensure activities align with Center, Cancer Center, and School of Medicine priorities.
Partner with Center leadership to develop, implement, and monitor strategic priorities, programs, and initiatives.
Oversee complex Center programs and projects, including coordination of resources, timelines, stakeholders, and deliverables.
Monitor progress toward Center goals and identify opportunities to improve operations, effectiveness, and overall program impact.
Develop and maintain appropriate reporting, metrics, and processes to support leadership decision-making and accountability.

Stakeholder Engagement, Communications, and Program Development (25%):

Serve as a key operational partner to Center leadership and maintain effective relationships with faculty, researchers, staff, donors, administrative partners, and other internal and external stakeholders.
Support the effective functioning of Center governance, committees, and advisory groups, including planning, coordination, communication, and follow-up.
Oversee Center communications and reporting efforts in collaboration with appropriate Cancer Center and University partners.
Provide programmatic oversight for major Center activities, events, and initiatives, ensuring they align with strategic priorities and are executed effectively.
Support the development of new programs, partnerships, and opportunities that advance the mission and impact of assigned Centers of Excellence.
Contribute to the development of shared approaches and best practices as the Cancer Center’s Centers of Excellence portfolio grows and evolves.

Financial and Resource Management (20%):

Oversee the financial management and resource planning for assigned Centers of Excellence in partnership with Center leadership and Cancer Center Finance.
Lead budget planning, monitoring, forecasting, and financial reporting to support effective stewardship of Center resources.
Ensure financial activities align with institutional requirements, funding restrictions, and Center priorities.
Identify financial risks, resource needs, and opportunities and provide information and recommendations to support leadership decision-making.
Oversee financial and business processes that support Center programs, initiatives, and operations.

Research Program Management (15%):

Support the coordination and advancement of research priorities and initiatives associated with assigned Centers of Excellence.
Partner with investigators, Center leadership, and Cancer Center research teams to support alignment of research activities with Center goals.
Facilitate collaboration and communication across clinical, translational, and basic science research stakeholders.
Support appropriate tracking, reporting, and evaluation of Center-related research activity and outcomes.
Identify opportunities to strengthen research collaboration, infrastructure, and program development within assigned Centers of Excellence.

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

The University of Colorado Cancer Center stands at the forefront of cancer research and patient care in Colorado. As the state's only National Cancer Institute (NCI) designated Comprehensive Cancer Center, we hold a prestigious distinction that acknowledges our exceptional contributions to the fields of research, clinical trials, prevention, and cancer control. Our guiding vision is clear: "prevent and conquer cancer. Together." At the heart of our mission is the work to “unite our community to overcome cancer through innovation, discovery, prevention, early detection, multidisciplinary care, and education.”

Our more than 300 members, made up of renowned physicians and researchers, conduct patient-centered research to develop innovative, state-of-the-art technologies, and treatments. Crucial to this work is the nearly 300 staff members who help expand the reach of the CU Cancer Center. Our expertise across cancer types helps us provide world-class treatment for common cancers, while offering hope for many patients with difficult or aggressive cancers who have struggled to find treatment options elsewhere.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Annapurna Labs, Inc
jobs.description:
Description

Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon that powers AWS's machine learning infrastructure, including the Trainium and Inferentia chip families. Our next-generation ML accelerator is a multi-die chiplet using state-of-the-art packaging technology, and it is the most complex hardware program Amazon has undertaken. We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end program execution for this chip, from RTL freeze through tape-out and into production readiness.

This is not a status-reporting role. You will be the person who connects a sprawling set of engineering workstreams into a single coherent schedule, identifies the real critical path week to week, and drives the cross-functional decisions that keep the program on track. The program spans multiple concurrent silicon development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, external partners, and infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities

Own the integrated schedule and critical path analysis across multiple die tape-outs through engineering samples and production ramp. Understand dependency chains deeply enough to calculate the impact of any slip or pull-in, and update the timeline weekly with real data.

Drive the weekly chip status cadence by synthesizing inputs from RTL/DV, physical design, packaging, power, infrastructure, and post-silicon teams into a single view that tells leadership where we actually stand, including what is getting worse and what needs action.

Track verification convergence as a leading indicator by monitoring the progression from feature completion through RTL closure, bug trends, and regression pass rates by block. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive the engineering response before downstream milestones are affected.

Manage the external design partner interface, owning the netlist delivery calendar, tracking your partner's physical design timeline, and negotiating schedule trades with a clear understanding of downstream cost.

Drive infrastructure readiness and external IP delivery by partnering with compute and EDA platform teams on capacity planning, and tracking third-party PHY, memory interface, and controller IP deliveries against consuming blocks to escalate gaps before they become tape-out critical.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing verification convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug closure rates haven't flattened. You pull the DV lead and RTL owner into a quick sync to agree on a recovery plan before the weekly chip status review. In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects a netlist delivery shift from your external design partner, quantifying the downstream impact on tape-out timing. After lunch, you join an infrastructure capacity review to confirm that compute clusters can handle the regression load through freeze, then close out the day preparing an executive summary for an upcoming program milestone review.

About The Team

The Annapurna Labs ML Accelerator team builds the Trainium and Inferentia silicon that trains and serves machine learning models across AWS. We work at the intersection of chip architecture, physical design, verification, and infrastructure to deliver products that push the boundaries of performance and efficiency for our customers. Our team values people who bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details. If you want to shape how Amazon builds its most ambitious hardware and work alongside talented engineers solving real problems at scale, this is the role for you.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
Deep working knowledge of the chip development lifecycle: RTL verification milestones, physical design convergence, DFT, and timing closure.
Experience managing programs with external design partners and IP vendors where you don't control the resources but own the outcome.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with real dependency modeling — not just Gantt charts, but an understanding of which paths have float and which don't.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
Experience with multi-die / chiplet / advanced packaging programs (2.5D/3D integration).
Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
Experience driving infrastructure capacity planning for large-scale chip development programs.

You will be the person who connects a sprawling set of engineering workstreams into a single coherent schedule, identifies the real critical path week to week, and drives the cross-functional decisions that keep the program on track. The program spans multiple concurrent silicon development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, external partners, and infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities

Own the integrated schedule and critical path analysis across multiple die tape-outs through engineering samples and production ramp. Understand dependency chains deeply enough to calculate the impact of any slip or pull-in, and update the timeline weekly with real data.

Drive the weekly chip status cadence by synthesizing inputs from RTL/DV, physical design, packaging, power, infrastructure, and post-silicon teams into a single view that tells leadership where we actually stand, including what is getting worse and what needs action.

Track verification convergence as a leading indicator by monitoring the progression from feature completion through RTL closure, bug trends, and regression pass rates by block. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive the engineering response before downstream milestones are affected.

Manage the external design partner interface, owning the netlist delivery calendar, tracking your partner's physical design timeline, and negotiating schedule trades with a clear understanding of downstream cost.

Drive infrastructure readiness and external IP delivery by partnering with compute and EDA platform teams on capacity planning, and tracking third-party PHY, memory interface, and controller IP deliveries against consuming blocks to escalate gaps before they become tape-out critical.

A day in the life

You start your morning reviewing verification convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug closure rates haven't flattened. You pull the DV lead and RTL owner into a quick sync to agree on a recovery plan before the weekly chip status review. In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects a netlist delivery shift from your external design partner, quantifying the downstream impact on tape-out timing. After lunch, you join an infrastructure capacity review to confirm that compute clusters can handle the regression load through freeze, then close out the day preparing an executive summary for an upcoming program milestone review.

About The Team

The Annapurna Labs ML Accelerator team builds the Trainium and Inferentia silicon that trains and serves machine learning models across AWS. We work at the intersection of chip architecture, physical design, verification, and infrastructure to deliver products that push the boundaries of performance and efficiency for our customers. Our team values people who bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details. If you want to shape how Amazon builds its most ambitious hardware and work alongside talented engineers solving real problems at scale, this is the role for you.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience
Deep working knowledge of the chip development lifecycle: RTL verification milestones, physical design convergence, DFT, and timing closure.
Experience managing programs with external design partners and IP vendors where you don't control the resources but own the outcome.
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with real dependency modeling — not just Gantt charts, but an understanding of which paths have float and which don't.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
Experience with multi-die / chiplet / advanced packaging programs (2.5D/3D integration).
Familiarity with HBM integration, die-to-die interfaces, or high-speed serial subsystems.
Experience with leading-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
Background in ML accelerator or high-performance compute silicon.
Experience driving infrastructure capacity planning for large-scale chip development programs.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About The Role

We’re looking for a Technical Program Manager who can work across engineering, product, and business teams. You’ll bring the technical judgment to earn engineers’ trust and the ability to create clarity and momentum across complex programs. This is a hands-on role with executive visibility and direct impact on how Ramp’s engineering organization scales.

Lead large technical programs across engineering and partner teams, from infrastructure scaling to reliability and incident response.
Connect platform and product engineering teams, keep context flowing, surface dependencies, and drive effective execution.
Own programs from scoping and kickoff through delivery, measurement, and retrospective.
Partner with engineering leaders on roadmaps, identify how projects overlap or depend on one another, and keep programs aligned with organizational goals.
Help engineers, engineering managers, and partner teams communicate business and engineering priorities across the organization.
Strengthen Ramp’s incident response program by improving processes, facilitating retrospectives, and helping teams act on what they learn.
Help define how TPMs work at Ramp by setting standards, creating playbooks, and improving program practices.

What You’ll Need

5+ years of technical program management experience, ideally in a high-growth startup.
Hands-on fluency with AI tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, and a point of view on how they can improve day-to-day work and software development.
The ability to execute directly while improving how the broader team works.
A track record of building trust quickly and working effectively across teams.
A BA/BS in computer science, engineering, information systems, analytics, or another technical or analytical field.
Strong systems thinking: you can connect architecture, product, compliance, and timelines, and spot risks early.
Experience leading cross-functional programs toward ambitious goals with urgency and ownership.

Nice To Haves

Experience with cell-based or multi-region architectures, or international expansion.
Hands-on experience with infrastructure, CI/CD, or observability tools.
Experience leading reliability programs.
Experience building programs in rigorous, fast-moving organizations.
A background in software engineering.
Familiarity with how LLM-based systems are built and deployed, enough to have substantive conversations with the engineers building them.

Founded in 1952 by its member systems to provide a reliable, cost-based supply of electricity, Tri-State is now headquartered in Westminster, Colo., employing approximately 1,000 people across five states.

Tri-State's electricity is generated from coal, natural gas, hydropower, wind, and solar. This power reaches members via a transmission system that includes substation facilities, telecommunications sites and almost 6,000 miles of high voltage transmission lines.

As a member-owned and -governed cooperative, every member has a voice and an equal vote in the future of Tri-State.

You will own organization-level and company-level initiatives where success requires alignment across multiple pillars, executive stakeholders and, in many cases, multiple TPMs. You will be the person senior leadership turns to when the work has no obvious owner, the solution is not yet known and the consequences of getting it wrong are significant.
You will identify problems and opportunities before requirements exist, define the strategy, translate that strategy into an executable plan and drive alignment around the people, resources and commitments required to deliver it.
You will operate as a strategic advisor to senior product and engineering leadership, including the RTO SVP, CTO and their directs. You will tell leaders what they need to hear, surface risks before they become issues and help shape both short-term execution and long-term technical direction.
At this level, your scope extends beyond delivering an individual program. You will lead programs with multiple TPMs, establish mechanisms that improve execution across organizations and raise the standard for technical program management across Axon.
The Real-Time Operations team builds, deploys and maintains products for emergency responders, specifically built around the Axon Fusus platform. Because every second counts for our customers, any production outage, functional regression or performance degradation that lasts even a few minutes can have a real impact.
The ideal candidate combines deep technical judgment, strong executive presence and the ability to drive accountability across organizations without relying on direct authority.
Location:
Seattle

Sr. Director of Technical Program Management
Direct reports
: None

Lead Axon's most complex cross-organization technical programs, including initiatives that span multiple R&D pillars and business functions.
Own organization-level or company-level outcomes from early strategy and problem definition through execution, launch and post-production.
Lead programs involving multiple TPMs and establish clear ownership, operating mechanisms and accountability across the program.
Identify high-impact problems before requirements exist and translate them into strategy, technical direction and executable plans.
Drive alignment across engineering, product, business, legal, information security, policy and other company organizations.
Own program plans, schedules, resourcing strategies and change management across multiple organizations.
Drive company-level accountability for commitments, dependencies and critical milestones.
Foresee systemic risks and organizational dependencies and establish mechanisms that prevent them from becoming execution failures.
Define success metrics for large-scale initiatives and ensure leaders use those metrics to make roadmap and investment decisions.
Own or guide end-to-end technical requirements across complex systems and multiple engineering organizations.
Bring senior engineering leaders together on architecture, system boundaries and difficult technical trade-offs.
Challenge technical assumptions and ensure decisions involving data stores, caching, system architecture, technology stacks and business logic are made with long-term consequences in mind.
Lead strategic technical discussions around scalability, reliability, availability and operational resilience.
Advise Directors, VPs, SVPs and executive leaders on portfolio strategy, execution risk, prioritization and where TPM capacity should be applied.
Write and present strategy documents that shape the short- and long-term direction of your space.
Present strategy, execution health and technical trade-offs to the RTO SVP, company CTO and their directs.
Lead programs that move into novel or previously unexplored areas where solutions are unknown, risk is high and failure could have significant customer impact.
Lead initiatives that extend beyond R&D and require alignment across broader company organizations.
Define and standardize TPM artifacts, tools, operating mechanisms and role expectations across the organization.
Create mechanisms that improve decision-making, accountability and execution even when you are not directly involved.
Raise the bar for how Axon applies AI to accelerate execution, program management and organizational effectiveness.
Mentor Principal TPMs and other senior technical leaders.
Interview and calibrate candidates through Principal TPM, Staff Engineer and Director levels.
Educate leaders and teams across R&D on program management practice, technical execution and organizational mechanisms.
Work effectively across multiple teams, organizations and time zones.

What Success Looks Like
Within 90 days: You have taken ownership of a company-critical initiative or portfolio, developed a clear assessment of its actual state and surfaced risks, dependencies or structural issues that leadership is actively addressing.
Within 6 months: You have established strong cross-organization operating mechanisms, commitments are holding and senior leaders are using your strategy and reporting to make roadmap, resourcing and prioritization decisions.
Within 12 months: You have delivered meaningful results across organizations, created mechanisms that have scaled beyond your immediate programs and materially raised the effectiveness of technical program management across your space.

What You Bring
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Science or a related field. Master's or PhD optional.
12 to 15+ years of experience managing complex software or hardware/software delivery.
2 to 3 years of experience as a technical individual contributor, engineer or equivalent hands-on technical role, or comparable technical depth developed through your career.

About ITC Infotech:

ITC Infotech is a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC Limited, one of India's foremost private sector companies and a diversified conglomerate. The ITC Group, with a market capitalization of $65 billion, is globally recognized as a leader in sustainability. The group's vision is to achieve world-class performance and create growing value for both the Indian economy and its stakeholders. This vision is supported by core values such as Trusteeship, where professional managers hold the company in "trust" for its stakeholders; a strong Customer Focus; Respect for People; a commitment to Excellence; a pursuit of Innovation; and a strong Nation Orientation.

ITC Infotech's business philosophy is that business is at the center and technology is an enabler, as reflected in its tagline, "Business-friendly Solutions." The company offers a wide range of services and solutions across key business areas, including CIO Services (Automation, Digital Workplace, ERP), Digital Experience (Experience Transformation), and Product 4.0 (Product Lifecycle Management, Digital Manufacturing). In the last seven years, ITC Infotech has successfully doubled its revenue from $250 million to $500 million+ annually, with its EBIT improving from 8% to over 18%.

With this strong growth momentum, ITC Infotech is now embarking on its next journey, known as 'Next Orbit,' with the ambitious goal of reaching $1 billion in annual revenue within the next four years. The Americas region is a critical part of this charter and is expected to increase its contribution to total revenue from the current 35% to a range of 40% to 50%. Manufacturing is a key vertical for the group and ITC Infotech with BFSI, Retail, CPG, Travel, Transportation & Hospitality being others.

Role - Principal Technical Program Manager

Location - Vancouver, BC

Start Date - Immediate

Duration - Long Term

Job description:

We are seeking a visionary Principal Technical Program Manager (TPM) to define, shape, and steer the next-generation global technology portfolio across Merch Planning, Forecasting, Sizing, and Allocation systems. Operating at the highest echelon of strategic leadership within Global Product Technology, you will be the primary bridge connecting business vision to enterprise-scale technology architecture.

This role requires a distinguished industry expert who does not just manage programs, but engineers organizational transformation. You will own the architectural sequencing and execution strategies that transform retail planning lifecycles, inventory flow, and allocation algorithms into competitive market advantages. If you are a seasoned leader capable of orchestrating massive, cross-portfolio platform migrations, driving technical standardization, and influencing VP-level business decisions, you will thrive in this role.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy, Governance & Organizational Vision

Define the Global Roadmap: Partner with executive leadership to establish the 3-to-5-year global technology vision and execution roadmap for Merch Planning, Forecasting, Sizing, and Allocation.
Enterprise Portfolio Ownership: Champion end-to-end organizational alignment, capital allocation, and delivery excellence across multi-million dollar program portfolios.
Synchronize with Business Milestones: Ensure technological evolutions natively support global GTM gates, multi-million dollar buy cycles, and high-impact merchandising decision-making windows.

Strategic Thought Partnership & Retail Value Generation

Executive Co-Pilot: Serve as the definitive strategic advisor to Vice Presidents and senior directors of Merch Planning and Allocation, transforming business hypotheses into resilient, scalable platforms.
Value-Chain Optimization: Drive systemic, metric-based improvements across global pre-season planning (assortment, sizing curves, buy quantities) and in-season execution (dynamic reforecasting, sell-through optimization, dynamic store/DC routing).
Macro Tradeoff Engineering: Arbitrate highly complex business-tech tradeoffs (e.g., algorithmic forecast accuracy vs. operational responsiveness; localized automation vs. localized planner override).

System Architecture & Technical Decision Leadership

Drive Platform Modernization: Lead architectural decision-making, sequence global data flows, and steer critical integrations across foundational engines (e.g., SaaS planning tools like Anaplan, massive data warehouses like Snowflake, and proprietary AI/ML microservices).
Establish Decision Frameworks: Author and champion the technical evaluation frameworks used by engineering and product executives to make high-stakes build-vs-buy and deprecation decisions.
System-of-Systems Translator: Demystify highly technical, data-science and algorithmic models into tangible product features, and vice-versa, for non-technical stakeholders.

Elite Delivery Models & Operating System Design

Define How We Deliver: Design, deploy, and scale the operational delivery models used by hundreds of engineers and program managers globally.
Institutionalize Execution Standards: Pioneer cross-portfolio execution standards, ensuring backlog readiness, cross-team coordination, and resource allocation are tied directly to corporate-level business outcomes.
Pioneer continuous improvement frameworks that guarantee industry-leading delivery predictability and software validation rigor during critical business freeze periods (such as Peak Season).

Cross-Functional Orchestration & Downstream Protection

Single-Threaded Executive Owner: Act as the ultimate orchestrator uniting Merch Planning, Allocation, Core Software Engineering, Data Science, and Product Management.
Risk & Dependency Mitigator: Proactively map, manage, and mitigate hidden systemic dependencies across forecasting engines, sizing logic, allocation systems, and financial ledger outputs.
Guard Data Integrity: Champion enterprise-level data quality standards to ensure downstream planning tools receive pristine, high-fidelity inputs.

High-Stakes Incident & Operational Leadership

Executive Incident Commander: Lead the resolution of high-severity production failures impacting global planning or allocation outcomes, orchestrating rapid recovery across disparate engineering groups.
Root Cause Pioneer: Direct post-mortem processes to identify structural flaws in technology or operational processes, ensuring permanent remediation and platform self-healing.
SLA & Reliability Standardizer: Set and enforce strict operational SLAs, ensuring 99.9% uptime and reliability for business-critical decision systems.

Corporate Influence & Executive Communication

C-Suite Storyteller: Author and deliver boardroom-ready reports, roadmaps, and business cases that explicitly tie technology infrastructure spend to core financial outcomes (e.g., inventory turn, GMROI, margins).
Value-Driven Prioritization: Lead high-level prioritization forums, ensuring organizational energy is spent on high-impact initiatives rather than localized optimizations.

Talent Incubation & Scalable Mentorship

Raise the Organizational Bar: Build scalable organizational mechanisms (e.g., automated forecast validation structures, standard transition playbooks, cross-portfolio dependency mapping) to elevate operational matureness.
Nurture Future Leaders: Formally mentor and coach Staff, Senior, and Mid-level TPMs/PMs on how to think strategically, master technical architectures, and connect delivery output to core business value.

Required Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Leadership, or Enterprise Architecture, with at least 5+ years operating at a Principal, Director, or equivalent scale.
Domain Mastery: Proven track record of architecting and delivering massive enterprise portfolios within Merch Planning, Allocation, Supply Chain, or high-throughput Retail Tech systems.
Transformational Leadership: Demonstrated experience leading large, matrixed cross-functional engineering and data science teams to deliver complex, multi-year initiatives.
Algorithmic Insight: Comprehensive grasp of forecasting models, inventory optimization algorithms, size-curve profiling, and data-driven pipeline systems.
Elite Executive Influence: Masterful written and verbal communication style, with extensive experience presenting directly to VP, SVP, and C-suite executives.

Preferred Qualifications

System Integration: Direct experience designing/migrating enterprise-scale instances of Anaplan, custom allocation engines, or legacy planning tools.
Advanced Data Platforms: Deep technical familiarity with Snowflake, AWS/GCP data stacks, end-to-end ETL/ELT pipelines, and streaming data processing.
Pioneering AI/ML Implementation: Hands-on experience scaling machine-learning forecasting and optimization models from R&D to enterprise production environments.
Omnichannel Expertise: Deep background in complex, global omnichannel retail, apparel, or high-velocity logistics ecosystems.

Education

Master’s or Bachelor’s in Computer Science, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, Management Information Systems (MIS), or a deeply technical related field; or equivalent practical experience.

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. Infrastructure & Platform Services builds and runs the technology foundation for EA’s games. Our teams deliver the live services and backend infrastructure that are used to ship, scale, and operate secure, reliable game experiences for millions of players worldwide.

As a Technical Program Manager III on the Commerce & Identity team, you will lead complex, high-visibility technical programs and multi-workstream initiatives that span multiple engineering, product, and operational teams. In this role, you will be responsible for translating strategic technology priorities into predictable, scalable execution.

You will bring clarity to ambiguous technical environments, align roadmaps across teams, and proactively mitigate cross-system dependencies and risks. You will act as a force multiplier by bringing teams together across engineering, product, and operations to deliver measurable outcomes on time and at scale.

Process Optimization: Refine delivery methodologies and operational workflows to reduce friction and improve velocity without introducing unnecessary overhead.
Tailored Communication: Deliver clear, data-informed program updates and executive briefings tailored to varied audiences.

Scope of Experience: Demonstrated track record of leading complex, multi-workstream initiatives that require coordination across multiple interdependent engineering teams.
Technical Fluency: Solid understanding of modern software architecture, systems engineering, CI/CD, or technical operations, with the credibility to partner effectively with senior engineers and other technical stakeholders.
Dependency & Risk Management: Proven ability to proactively identify, track, and remediate cross-functional dependencies, risks, and technical blockers.
Stakeholder Influence: Strong capability to build alignment, resolve conflict, and influence outcomes across cross-organizational stakeholders without direct reporting authority.
Communication Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex technical updates for leadership and cross-functional partners.
Experience within large-scale gaming platforms, central technology operations, or enterprise cloud infrastructure is a plus.
Familiarity with agile, hybrid, and scaled delivery frameworks is a plus.
Experience developing custom dashboards, program health frameworks, and automated reporting tooling (e.g., Jira, PowerBI/Tableau) is a plus.
Familiarity with core digital commerce or identity and access management domains is a plus

jobs.description:
Job Summary

General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.

We have an exciting opportunity for a dynamic and self-driven Additive Manufacturing (AM) Project Manager in our AM department located in Poway, CA. This position will occupy a strategic role in the growth of AM at GA-ASI, by supporting current and next generation UAS platform development leveraging a variety of AM technologies and materials. This position will act as principal AM-related project management interface between the AM department and a wide range of internal programs and external customer-funded programs. Providing both project management and AM expertise skills, this role will be driving simultaneously several projects related to new AM applications, IRAD, CRAD, process improvement, communication, training program, as well as complex production-related projects while providing periodical updates to the working teams and to the leadership. This role is part of the AM department and will support the AM application engineering team in the development and management of technical project scope of work (SOW) plan and drive the project all the way through its completion. This role will have a major component of outward-facing interaction with external customers & partners, as well as with various internal engineering, quality, and program stakeholder teams across GA-ASI.

Although it is part of the Operations division, this position will be a key interface role between various other internal stakeholders such as Quality Engineering, Materials & Processes Engineering, Advanced Programs Management, Contracts and Procurement teams, Special Programs, Design Engineering, Service and Supply Chain management. It will also interface and work closely with multiple programs within the greater GA&A company (other divisions of GA). This position will be key to help integrate AM applications into GA-ASI’s products and processes, as part of the Center of Excellence mission statement. This position will provide the candidate with an opportunity to be at the forefront and a key contributor to the growth of plastics, metals, tooling and composites AM at GA-ASI, and participate to customer-funded AM programs.

JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Development and execution of AM technical project scope of work, plan, schedule and budget in support of the AM application development engineering team efforts, as well as for internal IRAD, externally-funded CRAD, process improvements, internal/external communication, training and production-related projects.
For assigned projects, act as primary Point of Contact (POC) between AM team and the several stakeholder teams/programs, providing a threshold level of AM expertise and representation throughout the execution of the projects, and coordinate participations of other Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) as needed.
Primary owner of AM-related project schedule and budget for assigned projects.
Driving communications, team alignment meetings and task coordination between all project stakeholders for AM-related projects, such as Manufacturing groups (machining, fabrication, integration, lamination, tooling engineering, etc.), Engineering groups (design, CFD, AIG, M&P, etc.), Quality and Metrology, Program offices, as well as with upper management.
Coordination of project execution with external suppliers/partners, as well as with DoD customer representatives when applicable.
Develop project tracking metrics and tools to facilitate reporting at all levels (working teams & leadership) and facilitate team growth.
Provide basic level of knowledge support on AM technologies as POC on a project team setting, while leveraging the AM team’s SMEs effectively as required. Technologies that should be supported by this role include (but not limited to): Fused Deposition Modeling – FDM, Selective Laser Sintering – SLS, Laser Powder Bed Fusion – LPBF, Binder Jet (sand), LSAM/BAAM, Direct Energy Deposition – Wired (DED-W), SLA, DLP, MJF and other AM technologies.
In collaboration with AM application engineering, keep records of project engagements, technical application best practices and lessons learned, and develop associated AM application growth metrics and best reporting practices for visibility at AM MFG group, stakeholders and leadership levels, up to executive level.
As needed, participate and drive communication initiative to promote AM knowledge transfer and awareness across the GA&A company.
In collaboration with AM application engineering, develop, maintain and communicate AM application library using intranet & AI tools/platforms.
Closely work with all internal AM technology work cells and AM Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, M&P, Stress engineering, and other internal stakeholders to ensure best project flow.
Support AM manufacturing engineers with their respective AM technology process improvement projects (as applicable) by developing strategies, plan, and help drive those to completion.
Work closely with procurement, production planning and logistics stakeholder in the execution of AM application projects.
Participate, support and drive multiple R&D projects connected to application development efforts.
Tracking project budgets and spending.

We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply.

Job Qualifications

Typically requires a Bachelors in Business Administration or related discipline and nine or more years of progressively complex experience in the project administration field with at least three of those years in project management. May substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education.
Demonstrated skills and experience in technical/engineering project management involving several different stakeholders (non-direct reports). A minimum of 3 years of direct engineering-related project management is required.
Basic working knowledge of AM industrial and prototyping technologies relevant to this role (e.g. FDM/FFF, SLS, LPBF/DLM/DMLS/DMLM, DED, EBM, BJT, and others) and their associated post-processing workflows.
Experience with Microsoft Office PowerPoint, Project, Excel and Visio. Alternate project management software solutions are equally valuable.
Ability to clearly and effectively communicate both verbally and in written form to both technical and non-technical audiences, especially regarding manufacturing processes, engineering issues and proposed changes, and quality issues and dispositions.
Demonstrated ability to form new partnerships, to connect with new stakeholders and to keep engaged.
Working knowledge of application development workflows for either aviation, aerospace, space, defense industries is highly valued.
Direct experience with trade study assessments, business case development and communication are highly preferred
Direct or tangential experience with AM production industrial environment (production-level AM), specifically with FDM and/or SLS and/or metal-LPBF and/or DED production printing is preferred.
Ability and interest in learning and mastering new AM technologies, in alignment with GA-ASI’s AM roadmap and upcoming applications.
Direct experience with conventional mechanical CAD designs, drawings and GD&T.
Working knowledge with part manufacturing process workflows, including but not limited to: production planning, engineering file controls, master routing, quality and inspection methodologies and technologies (e.g. CT scanning, other NDT, blue scanning, CMM, roughness, etc.).
Working knowledge of conventional manufacturing processes (complementary to AM processes, such as CNC machining, coating, plating, infiltrating, painting, injection molding, casting, investment casting, etc.) is a great advantage for this role.
Working knowledge and familiarity with AI-based solutions.
Demonstrated ability to handle multiple conflicting priorities and multiple concurrent projects.

Description

The Security Business Analyst, in this role will bridge the gap between traditional business analysis and a deep security foundation. Your mission is to ensure that business requirements for Client Identity and Access Management (CIAM) are aligned with stringent security controls and complex technical use cases. You will translate requirements from business stakeholders, development teams, and security experts to ensure all identity products across are both user-centric and technically sound. The Security Business Analyst is a critical thinker who understands that security is the foundation of client trust—a proactive problem-solver, comfortable navigating the nuances of authentication protocols, and skilled at ensuring a seamless, secure journey for every client. Pay

Responsibilities

CIAM Translation: Serves as the primary translator between business units and security engineering, turning complex client identity needs into feasible, secure solutions.
Project Delivery: Supports critical initiatives driving the delivery of the digital authentication strategy. Key initiatives include but are not limited to a Unified D2C Client Application, adoption of stronger and phishing resistant authentication, dynamic and assurance based fraud controls such as 2-way notifications, and expansion of Ping to strengthen enterprise fraud and identity tooling.
Access Risk Analysis: Focuses on analyzing access management, encryption, and authentication practices to identify security risks within client-facing platforms (e.g., Virtual Assistant, Retail Banking).
Standardization: Builds a standardized set of security product requirements for DIAM and produces metrics to report performance against those requirements.
Process Enhancement: Researches and analyzes improvement opportunities within identity workflows to facilitate efficiency enhancements that don't compromise security.
Innovate and set the vision for the Client Identity product, managing and leading the roadmap delivery at the component/phase level.
Manage activities for the identity product through its entire lifecycle, including defining requirements and liaising with engineers and UX designers for the Digital Project.
Support the integration and strengthening of fraud detection systems through new tools to help reduce monetary fraud losses.
Act as an emissary of the Identity, Application and Offensive Security team working to promote strong partnerships with teams and stakeholders that are dependent on our services.

Qualifications

3–5 years of Business Analysis experience, with a proven focus on Identity & Access Management (IAM) or Digital Identity.
Foundational understanding of authentication protocols (OIDC, SAML, OAuth) and data privacy regulations.
Core Business Process Management - monitoring business processes and improving them over time.
Customer Research & Journey Mapping - Planning, leading, and conducting user research and usability studies.
Strategic Planning - Documenting and establishing direction of a vision and roadmap for a product.
Identity Management: Deep understanding of Identifying, authenticating, and authorizing clients across digital applications.
Access Management: Mastery of granting authorized access while preventing unauthorized entry through robust MFA and SSO strategies.
Security Risk Analysis: Ability to conduct risk-based analysis of client behavior and network usage to identify potential vulnerabilities.
Systems Thinking: Understanding how identity components interlink with core banking systems, cloud infrastructure, and third-party migrations.
Data & Analytics: Proficiency Technical Skills:
in producing metrics and dashboards to report on authentication success rates and security event trends.
Experience with Design Thinking, User Scenario Tools and Customer Research & Journey Mapping.
Interpersonal and Leadership Skills:
Stakeholder Management: Expertly manages expectations and prioritizes deliverables for high-impact digital initiatives.
Vision Design & Delivery: Collaborates with Product Owners to design a secure vision for the client identity roadmap.
Critical Thinking: Evaluates every requirement through a security lens, ensuring that "user-centric" also means "stringently protected."
Verbal & Written Communication: Skilled at "storytelling"—explaining the technical "why" behind security controls to non-technical business partners.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
Completion of or progress toward IIBA certification (CCBA/CBAP) and/or security certifications such as CompTIA Security+ or CIAM-specific training are considered an asset

The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced ICT / Low Voltage & Controls Project Manager to lead the delivery of network infrastructure, structured cabling, monitoring systems, and controls integration on hyperscale and mission-critical data center construction projects. This role is responsible for managing the full lifecycle of ICT, low-voltage, and controls scopes, from design coordination and installation planning through commissioning and final turnover. These systems form the operational backbone of the facility, supporting building management systems, electrical monitoring, network infrastructure, and operational telemetry.

What you will do?

Project Delivery

Manage execution of ICT, Low Voltage, and Controls infrastructure across hyperscale data center builds.
Lead delivery of structured cabling systems (fiber and copper), pathways, cable management, network cabinets, and monitoring infrastructure.
Coordinate installation of controls interfaces supporting BMS, EPMS, and equipment telemetry.
Develop and manage ICT/Controls schedules aligned with electrical energization, mechanical startup, and commissioning milestones.
Coordinate closely with GC leadership, electrical contractors, mechanical trades, commissioning agents, and controls integrators.

Controls Integration

Manage installation readiness for PLC interfaces, control panels, sensors, monitoring equipment, and communication gateways.
Coordinate integration between network infrastructure and facility controls platforms.
Work with controls vendors and system integrators to ensure proper interface between field devices and monitoring systems.
Support troubleshooting and resolution of controls communication and integration issues during commissioning.

Scope & Risk Management

Identify and resolve design gaps, scope conflicts, and cross-trade interface risks.
Issue and manage RFIs related to ICT, monitoring, and controls integration.
Maintain strict control of scope boundaries and change management.
Prevent commissioning delays by ensuring systems are installation-ready before vendor mobilization.

Vendor & Quality Management

Manage low voltage subcontractors, controls integrators, and specialty vendors.
Ensure compliance with project specifications, owner standards, NEC, TIA, and BICSI guidelines.
Verify testing results, labeling standards, and documentation accuracy.
Maintain strict quality standards in uptime-sensitive environments.

Commissioning & Turnover

Lead ICT and Controls readiness for commissioning.
Coordinate testing activities with commissioning teams and equipment vendors.
Ensure completion of as-built documentation, labeling records, and turnover packages.
Support issue resolution through final commissioning and project closeout

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management or related field; will consider minimum of 5 years practical experience
Minimum of 5 years of professional construction experience
GC experience required, green field experience preferred
Three or more years of Project Management experience in commercial construction practices and procedures. Industrial construction preferred, not required
Strong working knowledge of construction methodologies, CSI building codes, and industry best practices
Experience with Microsoft Office suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, MS Project preferred but not required), BlueBeam, Revit, Design Reviewer, and Adobe Professional
Construction Management software use experience with ProCore is required, familiarity with P6 scheduling software, Microsoft Project are preferred but not required (i.e.: document control and schedule software, etc.)

jobs.description:
Workflow Transformation Analyst – Process Innovation COE

Role Overview

Pearson is fundamentally reimagining how educational products are built, from first concept through learner impact. The Workflow Transformation Analyst is a driving force in that reinvention—a hands-on change agent who doesn’t just map today’s processes but architects tomorrow’s. Embedded within our new Process Innovation COE, you will partner with Product Management, Engineering, Content Development, Production, QA, and Operations to dismantle legacy bottlenecks, design AI-native workflows, and stand up scalable operating models that dramatically accelerate speed to market and quality at scale. If you’re the kind of person who sees a broken process and can’t rest until it’s been rebuilt from the ground up—this role was made for you.

What You’ll Own & Drive

Tear apart end-to-end workflows across content creation, production, QA, and release—then redesign them for radical efficiency, eliminating handoff waste and compressing cycle times.

Architect next-generation operating models and workflow blueprints that become the gold standard across Pearson’s product portfolio—not incremental tweaks, but step-change transformations.

Be the tip of the spear on AI-native workflow design—identify and implement high-impact automation opportunities using generative AI, agentic AI, and intelligent tooling to replace manual, error-prone work with scalable, self-improving systems.

Drive the delivery of digital content and online course programs with urgency and accountability—owning outcomes, not just timelines.

Own the full initiative lifecycle—planning, dependency mapping, risk mitigation, and delivery health—with a bias toward unblocking teams and accelerating momentum, not administering status reports.

Rally and align matrixed, cross-functional teams around shared transformation goals—building coalitions, not just coordinating calendars.

Lead high-energy workshops, transformation sprints, and workflow deep dives that produce concrete, implementable change—not slide decks that gather dust.

Hunt for and unlock cross-Business Unit synergies—reusable patterns, shared tooling, and common operating models that multiply impact beyond any single team.

Establish transparent, data-driven progress tracking that keeps transformation initiatives honest and on the rails—surfacing risks early and driving corrective action fast.

What Makes You a Fit

Deep expertise in workflow design, process transformation, and operating model architecture—you’ve redesigned how work gets done, not just documented it.

A track record of leading cross-functional transformation initiatives in complex, matrixed organizations—managing dependencies, breaking logjams, and shipping results.

Exceptional communication and influence skills—you can sell a new way of working to skeptics and energize teams around bold change.

Hands-on fluency with Agile, Scrum, or hybrid delivery models—and the judgment to know when to flex the framework.

Proficiency with modern workflow and collaboration tooling (Jira, Smartsheet, Confluence, SharePoint, Teams) and a hunger to push beyond them.

Working knowledge of AI/ML concepts and practical experience applying generative AI and prompt engineering to real business workflows.

Technical literacy (HTML, scripting, or low-code platforms) sufficient to prototype and validate automation ideas—you don’t just spec it, you prove it.

You thrive in ambiguity, move fast when others are paralyzed, and bring contagious energy to high-stakes transformation work.

Education

Bachelor’s degree required (or equivalent practical experience).

How We’ll Measure Impact

Measurable reduction in end-to-end cycle times for content creation and product delivery.

Elimination (not just reduction) of manual, error-prone steps through automation and AI-enabled workflows.

New operating models adopted at scale across multiple Business Units—not pilot-only wins.

On-time, high-quality delivery of transformation initiatives with clear before/after evidence of impact.

Stakeholders actively requesting your involvement on their next initiative—the ultimate proof of value.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Total Rewards
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Total Rewards Strategy & Enablement (TR S&E) team translates people strategy into business impact, building the infrastructure, programs, and systems that make Total Rewards work at scale. We're a small, high-leverage team that bridges strategy and execution, partnering with People leadership and cross-functional teams across Finance, Legal, and the business to turn ambiguous problems into durable programs.

What you’ll do

Stripe's Total Rewards programs span compensation, benefits, equity, internal mobility/immigration, and mergers and acquisitions (M&A), each with cross-functional dependencies, regulatory stakes, and direct impact on the Stripes they affect. Delivering these programs well takes a Project Manager who develops real subject matter depth, engages with pillar leads as a strategic partner, and brings structure to decisions that aren't always clear-cut.

We're hiring a Project Manager to own high-priority Total Rewards projects and programs end to end. You'll work closely with our Benefits, Compensation, Equity, Talent Mobility, and M&A pillars, building expertise in how these programs work and what it takes to land them well. Some programs have established playbooks you'll sharpen; others are less defined and will need you to help shape the approach before you execute it. Across all of them, you'll identify dependencies early, proactively surface and mitigate risks, and keep complex, multi-stakeholder work moving toward clear outcomes. This is a high-leverage individual contributor role for someone who brings both rigor and judgment to every project they own.

Responsibilities

Own end-to-end project management for high-profile cyclical and transformational Total Rewards projects, from intake and scoping through go-live and handoff to program owners
Advise and embed with project teams across the Total Rewards and People portfolio, raising the quality bar and building PM capability across the extended team, not just doing the work yourself
Build subject matter expertise across Benefits, Compensation, Equity, Talent Mobility, and M&A — becoming a reliable strategic thought partner to pillar teams on program decisions, not just a tracker of status
Build, automate, and continuously improve the infrastructure that makes program management repeatable and scalable: intake frameworks, project plan templates, SOPs, playbooks, and handoff checklists for common program types
Leverage AI tools in your daily work and the team's workflows, using them to accelerate synthesis, drafting, stakeholder communications, and documentation, and actively identifying new opportunities to work faster and better
Drive cross-functional alignment across People and key partner functions (Legal, Finance, Corporate Technology, and others), creating shared visibility into priorities, dependencies, and blockers
Tackle complex, ambiguous program questions with rigor and independence, owning work from problem definition through final recommendation — including defining the approach, monitoring progress, identifying risks early, and putting mitigation in place before issues land
Surface patterns and gaps across the program portfolio, translating observations into structured analysis and recommendations for People leadership

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

7+ years of People project, program, or operations management experience, including at least 3 years driving multi-stakeholder, cross-functional programs end to end, ideally at a scaling or global company
A track record of building from scratch: you've created processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure where none existed before, not just improved what was already in place
Excellent written communication: you can produce an executive update, a stakeholder decision memo, and a practitioner playbook with equal fluency
Strong stakeholder management across senior cross-functional partners: you drive results with a balance of urgency and thoughtfulness, and know when to push, when to align, and when to escalate
AI expertise: you default to AI tools for synthesis, drafting, analysis, and communications, and you proactively design workflows that help the team move faster and operate at scale.
Analytical fluency: you can work with data to build a credible narrative, identify patterns across a program portfolio, and make recommendations grounded in evidence
A users-first mindset: you obsess over the Stripe employee experience and the operator experience, not just the project/program artifacts

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with change management frameworks (such as Prosci ADKAR) and judgment about when to apply structured change management vs. lighter-touch approaches
Experience building and deploying enablement materials or training resources for cross-functional teams
Experience in Total Rewards, People Operations, or an adjacent HR domain
Familiarity with PM and collaboration tools (Asana, Jira, or similar)
Familiarity with Total Rewards or HR systems (such as Workday, equity administration platforms, or benefits administration tools)
PMP, Lean/Six Sigma, or comparable structured-program training

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $127,600 - $191,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

This role combines program ownership with hands-on instructor-led training, ensuring both internal Axon teams and external law enforcement customers can successfully adopt Fusus workflows. Job Summary

The Intelligence Analyst supports Inspection Service criminal programs, including, but not limited to, mail fraud, narcotics, prohibited mailings, money laundering, and organized crime. This position will provide analytical support services to an investigative support service center focused on complex criminal investigations by incorporating information from multiple sources to develop leads and comprehensive targeting plans. The analyst shall be capable of using technology solutions to actively search, analyze, prioritize, and present information for USPIS investigators.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

General knowledge of federal statutes.
Experience supporting criminal investigations.
Financial analysis and understanding of financial regulatory processes.
Experience with Bank Secrecy (BSA) data
Experience tracking money laundering and structuring activities of criminal organizations.
Extensive experience in analyzing data and interpreting patterns or trends using appropriate analytical techniques and methods.
Proficiency conducting research on the internet and commercial as well as public databases.
Experience with mapping platforms such as ArcGIS.
Experience with phone toll analysis conducted using PLX or PenLink.
Experience using analytical tools and visualization software such as the i2 Analysts Notebook, Microstrategy, Tableau, and QLIK.
Experience working on time-sensitive projects, often under pressure with the ability to multi-task various tasks at the same time.
Ability to work independently, take initiative, to complete assignments within reasonable and specified time frames.
Ability to participate in court proceedings, if required.
Foreign languages desirable, including Spanish.

Work Duties And Tasks

Included, but not limited to:

Intelligence Gathering and Assessment

Evaluate information from a variety of sources to include agency databases, investigative resources, social media, chats, forums, dark net, Tor network, news feeds, internet relay chats and other sources of data openly available on the Internet. Perform a prioritized assessment of the data to identify the most critical and reliable data in order to identify: criminal activity, monetization methods, locations, accounts, services, travels, email addresses, IP addresses and other pattern of life data in an effort to determine attribution.

Data Analysis

Analyze data to identify and interpret patterns and trends, assess data quality and eliminate irrelevant data; present findings in reports and presentations in non-technical terminology to various audiences.

Reporting Responsibilities

Responsible for documenting and reporting analytical results, creating graphic displays and reports that present clear and concise representations of the information analyzed; and disseminating data as required by the assigned task(s).

Preparatory Investigation

Assist Inspectors with developing intelligence for criminal investigations. Prepare investigative research for investigations and prosecution. Compile background information, USPIS sourced information, and intelligence from third-party entities such as commercial databases, law enforcement agencies, and victims.

Asset identification

Develop the required level of proof needed to seize and forfeit assets via civil, criminal and administrative forfeiture processes; utilize compliance databases such as the USPS Bank Secrecy Act Database, and FINCEN to identify and locate assets. Assist with subpoena content creation, property/vehicle title & lien review and open-source searches of relevant financial data and asset ownership.

Minimum Qualifications & Skills

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university which will assist in this position’s requirements and duties.
A minimum of five years of experience reviewing information, conducting analysis, performing research, and communicating effectively both orally and in writing.
Experience in supporting criminal investigations is strongly desired.
Significant demonstrated experience may be considered in lieu of formal education.

Aboud Gartner Information Security:

Gartner Information Security enables the business to move quickly and confidently by protecting our people, data, and ideas. We are a global team of defenders, investigators, engineers, and lifelong learners who solve complex security challenges together.

You will join an inclusive, security-first culture where expertise is shared, thoughtful challenge is encouraged, and strong ideas can come from anyone. About the role:

We are seeking a Senior Security Analyst to help strengthen our global Security Operations capability. You will independently handle complex investigations, improve detection and response, and help protect Gartner’s people, data, and intellectual property. You will independently handle complex investigations, improve detection and response, and help protect Gartner’s people, data and intellectual property.

This is a hands-on role for someone who combines strong technical capability with sound judgement, clear communication, and a drive to improve how a global SOC operates. You will be an experienced investigator, a trusted technical escalation point for other analysts, a mentor and a builder of better ways to detect, investigate, and respond.

Pls note
: Our Security Operations Centre (SOC) operates on a continuous 24x7 model to protect global systems and support business needs across time zones.

What you will need:

Relevant experience: 3 to 5 years of experience in information security, security operations, incident response, or an equivalent hands-on role.
Investigation capability: Proven experience triaging and investigating cybersecurity events and incidents, prioritizing effectively and working confidently in a time-sensitive environment.
Technical depth: Hands-on experience across SIEM or XDR, EDR, email security, web proxy and digital forensics and incident response.
Cloud and data skills: Experience investigating AWS, Azure or GCP environments and working with SPL, KQL, SQL or comparable query languages.
Proactive defense: Practical threat-hunting experience; red or purple team exposure is advantageous.
Automation mindset: Ability to automate Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar technologies and identify opportunities to reduce repetitive operational work.
Influence and communication: Strong written and verbal communication, documentation, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to explain technical issues clearly and support other analysts.

What will you do:

Investigate complex incidents: Independently investigate security incidents from initial triage through scoping, containment, remediation and closure, escalating high-impact events and coordinating with the Lead Security Analyst when needed.
Analyze deeply: Correlate evidence across SIEM, EDR, cloud, email, proxy, network and supporting telemetry to determine root cause, scope, impact and remediation.
Communicate clearly: Produce concise, high-quality investigation notes, incident reports and actionable outcomes for technical teams and business stakeholders.
Improve detection and response: Develop and tune detection content, investigative workflows and playbooks aligned with MITRE ATT&CK, the Cyber Kill Chain and other relevant frameworks.
Build and automate: Develop practical tools and automation that reduce repetitive work, accelerate investigations, and improve SOC effectiveness.
Hunt proactively: Identify malicious behavior, vulnerabilities, control gaps, misconfigurations and anomalous activity across endpoint, network and cloud environments.
Support the team: Act as an escalation point for other analysts, share knowledge, and help strengthen technical and investigative capability.
Drive continuous improvement: Contribute practical ideas that improve processes, demonstrate operational excellence, and advance the maturity of the global SOC.

What you will love about working here:

Visible impact: Help strengthen the maturity of a global SOC while protecting a business that operates on a worldwide scale.
Meaningful ownership: Take responsibility for the technical investigation of complex incidents, influence outcomes, and see strong ideas move from concept to implementation.
Modern security challenges: Work across diverse technologies and environments, supported by tools and investment that enable you to do your best work.
Growth through collaboration: Learn with skilled colleagues who value curiosity, knowledge sharing, thoughtful challenges, and continuous improvement.
Autonomy with support: Have the freedom to improve how we work, backed by a global team committed to shared success.

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

We're hiring a Security Risk Specialist, who will help run and shape our risk management program and treatment plans, enabling risk and control owners and security teams to keep risk at an acceptable level as the business grows. You will work cross-functionally to achieve business goals by running risk assessments and reporting, supporting exception requests when a policy can't be met, and helping automate the tooling and processes that keep our risk register accurate and trustworthy. Collaborate and report widely within our GRC and security teams and across the business
